payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: In the edited image, can the source-image paper and cup be identified, and is there visible progress toward stuffing that paper into that cup without the paper already being stuffed inside?
node.criteria: Pass only if the edited image provides enough evidence to identify the same paper and cup shown in the source, shows movement or placement advancing the paper toward or into the cup, and s1 has not established completion. Fail only if both objects are identifiable and there is visibly no progress toward the requested placement, or s1 establishes completion. Unknown if either object's identity or the relevant progress relation cannot be established.
node.binding: Progress counts only when it advances stuffing the source-image paper into the source-image cup. Do not infer absence of progress from uncertain object identity or proximity.

node_traces.evidence: The source shows a white paper and a blue cup, but the edited image shows a hand holding a blue printed item near a reddish object. The source paper and cup cannot be reliably identified in the edited image, so progress toward stuffing the paper into the cup cannot be established.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too vague: “paper (...) stuffed into the cup” omits the source-to-edit identity and the distinction between completion and partial progress. Make the typed criteria explicitly assess whether the edited scene shows the source paper and cup (allowing reasonable appearance changes), whether the paper is visibly inserted into the cup, and whether any identifiable part of the requested action has progressed without completion. Here, the edited image shows a hand holding a blue printed item near a reddish object; it does not visibly establish the source paper or blue cup, insertion, or progress. That is unresolved visual evidence—not proof that no change occurred—so do not force the reference “no” by relaxing the rubric or treating unidentifiable objects as absent. The high-confidence unresolved judgments warrant checking whether the evidence prompts support calibrated identity matching and partial-progress assessment. The trace is valid and queried, with no transport, schema, or dependency failure indicated; preserve the existing completion/no-progress/partial/unknown logic and improve the binding’s evidence criteria rather than changing routing or adding dependencies.
